An optional visit to the Larco Museum costs $65 per person.

Archaeologist Rafael Larco Hoyle founded the museum in 1926. The collection is housed in an 18th-century colonial mansion on the site of an earlier pre-Columbian structure. Around 45,000 objects introduce you to the civilisations that flourished in Peru long before the Incas.

The galleries display ceramics, textiles, gold and silver objects, ritual items and archaeological finds. The collection highlights Moche ceramics, including pieces with erotic imagery that offer a glimpse into how ancient Peruvians understood life and fertility.
After the tour, transfer to the airport for your international flight.
Road to the airport, with the terminal and control tower in Lima, Peru
Lima: the airport access road, terminal and control tower
A traveller and clouds reflected in the mirror-like surface of the Uyuni Salt Flat, Bolivia
Uyuni: walking through shallow water amid reflections of the sky and mountains

Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu open the Peruvian leg of your trip. The road through the Andes takes you to Puno, and a catamaran crosses Lake Titicaca to the Island of the Sun. From La Paz, you fly to the Uyuni Salt Flat, spend a day in its wide white expanse and watch the sun set over tea. After visiting La Paz and the Valley of the Moon, you return to Lima.

## Guides and flights

An English-speaking guide accompanies the excursions in the itinerary, except for the Lake Titicaca crossing and Uyuni. We confirm the guide language for these sections when you book.

The included flights are Lima → Cusco and La Paz → Uyuni → La Paz. The day-by-day itinerary includes a La Paz → Lima flight. We confirm whether it is included and what it costs before payment.
